beats: Hook: before a 70-billion-parameter model reads a single word, its training state already weighs about a terabyte.
The bill: FP16 weights 2 B + gradients 2 B + FP32 Adam state 12 B (two moments and a master copy) = 16 B per parameter; the optimizer state is the bulk (T-shirts vs winter coats).
The waste: plain data parallelism packs the same full suitcase onto every GPU.

Not tensor parallelism: ZeRO never splits the work (four people building one tent together is TP, L06-03); every GPU still cooks its own whole meal on its own data and only borrows the recipe pages it does not carry.
ZeRO-1: shard the optimizer state (one coat each); ReduceScatter + AllGather cost the same as one AllReduce: free.
ZeRO-2: also shard the gradients, dropping each layer's after it is reduced; strictly better?

ZeRO-3 / FSDP: shard the weights too (daypacks); copy each layer's weights in just in time, use them, throw the copy away: about 1.5x the traffic, hidden by handing over the next card early (prefetch).
Numbers: 70B on 16 GPUs: ~310, ~187, ~65 GiB per GPU under ZeRO-1, 2, 3 (one H100 has 80 GB): only the last fits the cabin-bag frame.

Twist: the big pre-training runs mostly use ZeRO-1: pipelines add up gradients over many micro-batches (coins in the jar), and ZeRO-2/3 would have to reduce-scatter after every one (a bank run per coin).
Limit: past a point more DP means tiny work per GPU and talk that cannot hide; other parallelism takes over (L06).
